description: Restoring Rangelands in Northern New Mexico with Keyline Design is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USFWS, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. Many factors, including drought, heavy livestock grazing, and mono-crop agriculture, have decreased the infiltration rate of the coarse-loamy soils prevalent in Northern New Mexico. Keyline design uses the natural ridges and contours of a property’s topography to slow, spread, and sink rainwater. Coverage: New Mexico (2024). The toolkit gives New Mexico as the location, 2024 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
